mode: Ask once, allow two passes, or turn reviews off.
no_prose_em_dash: Allow list separators and empty table values.
model_review: Use your Hermes model. Adds a review request per pass.
min_words: Default: 200 words. Use 0 to check shorter text.
vale_mode: Add Vale findings when a document is reviewed, using the executable you approved with the Vale tool.
vale_min_alerts: Show a summary after this many findings.
vale_path: Leave blank to find Vale automatically.
exceptions: Write one rule per line as rule_name: file_pattern, file_pattern. For example, signposting: README.md, docs/** skips that check in README files and docs folders. Use * in filename patterns, or all: pattern to skip every check in matching files. Leaving this blank adds no exceptions.
tell_closing_offers: Offers such as ‘Let me know if you need more.’
tell_hedges: Several qualifiers without a clear claim.
tell_signposting: ‘Here’s what you need to know’ and similar lead-ins.
tell_filler: ‘Due to the fact that’ instead of ‘because.’
tell_trailing_qualifiers: Endings such as ‘for the most part.’
tell_negation_positive: ‘It isn’t about X. It’s about Y.’
tell_negation_triads: Repeated contrasts that introduce a bigger claim.
tell_verdict_openers: ‘The honest answer’ before the actual answer.
tell_cliche_openers: Openings such as ‘In today’s fast-paced world.’
tell_bold_pseudo_headings: Whole lines of bold text outside normal headings.
tell_bold_lead_bullets: Lists where most items begin with a bold label.
tell_buzzwords: Dense runs of words such as ‘delve’ and ‘tapestry.’
tell_banned_words: Terms you chose to flag in your writing profile.
tell_em_dashes: Keep list separators and empty table values.
tell_candor_frames: ‘To be fully transparent’ before a routine point.
tell_objection_frames: ‘Some might say’ without an objection to answer.
tell_emphasis_crutches: Statements of importance without a consequence.
tell_dev_slogans: Claims such as ‘It just works’ or ‘sane defaults.’
tell_wh_openers: Repeated ‘What makes this hard is’ constructions.
tell_future_narrative: ‘One of the most important’ without a clear outcome.
tell_negative_listing: Lists of what something is not
Repeated negatives before the positive claim.
tell_number_inflation: ‘Five things to know’ and similar framing.
tell_hashtag_stuffing: Six or more tags in one piece of writing.
tell_over_compression: Arrows and symbols used in place of sentences.
tell_rule_of_three: Many short, parallel groups of three.
tell_same_openers: Several sentences starting with the same word.
tell_staccato_runs: Three or more very short sentences in a row.
tell_question_runs: Repeated questions outside interviews and FAQs.
tell_bare_bullet_runs: Five or more short bullets without complete claims.
tell_vague_authority: Claims attributed to ‘experts’ without naming them.
tell_real_actual: Claims such as ‘real value’ without a named contrast.
tell_launch_copy: ‘Say hello to’ and similar product announcements.
tell_assistant_residue: Pleasantries, stock offers, and capability disclaimers.
tell_template_residue: TBD, sample fields, and bracketed instructions.
tell_tool_fingerprints: AI-referrer parameters added to a URL.
tell_citation_residue: Internal citation codes left in the published text.
tell_reasoning_residue: Text such as ‘Let me think step by step.’
tell_fake_casual_props: Stage directions such as ‘checks notes’ or ‘mic drop.’
tell_crowd_contrast: Claims about what ‘everyone else’ was still doing.
tell_hedged_enumeration: ‘A few things to consider’ before the answer.
tell_scar_tissue: Repeated options introduced only to dismiss them.
tell_lingering_attention: ‘I keep coming back to this’ without a reason.
tell_parallel_reasons: Three sentences in a row using ‘because’ or ‘when.’
tell_title_case_headings: Repeated title case where sentence case would fit.
tell_decorative_headers: Repeated emoji headings in formal writing.
tell_label_periods: A bold noun label ending with a period.
tell_stranded_auxiliary: Repeated endings such as ‘the data didn’t.’
tell_colon_triples: Repeated colon openings into groups of three.
tell_self_labeling_significance: Calling a point ‘the clever part’ after making it.
tell_negation_chain: Phrases such as ‘No fluff, no filler, no jargon.’
tell_empty_concession: Repeated praise followed by an unnamed challenge.
tell_stock_reaction_frame: Repeated ‘What surprised me most was’ openings.
tell_tier1a: Words to inspect for vague or inflated meaning.
tell_tier1b: Longer or formal phrases with plainer alternatives.
tell_tier2: Two or more terms in the same paragraph.
tell_tier3: Heavy repetition of one broad descriptive word.
tell_tier3_phrases: The same phrase twice, or three stock phrases.
